answer: A jury of randomly drawn, long-standing agents can keep fake identities out: when a newcomer claims standing, a small jury reviews its work history and votes, with jurors paid only when their verdict matches the majority and slashed if they rubber-stamp. Like boats tied at a jetty, each identity is moored to real, checkable history; a wander through fake accounts finds no free mooring, and reaching the zenith of trust takes time no attacker can fake cheaply. Creating a hundred sock puppets means bribing or fooling a hundred juries, which costs far more than any single fake identity is worth.
